initiative.title: [I17] Cutover Readiness: Every Known Skill Fix Lands Before the Extraction

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: type:initiative
labels.description: A track that holds epics

labels.name: priority: 2
labels.description: Queue rank. A larger number runs first.

labels.name: theme:planning

initiative.body:
## Overview

Every Work Planner skill fix found before the skill leaves workflow-server is merged into workflow-server's `workspace` branch before the skill's extraction is cut, so the repository the skill moves to starts with every known fix. The goal the reviews test against: each fix found before the cutover is delivered in workflow-server ahead of the extraction, and the extraction carries it.

## Problem

Faults found in the skill before its move have no plan that the move respects.

- **A late fix misses the move.**
  The skill is extracted to prosiform-skills with its content unchanged, so a fix merged into `workspace` after the extraction reaches only the copy workflow-server drops.
- **Known faults are open.**
  Closing the skill's own initiative exposed faults in [Plan Mode](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L42-L43), the [format check](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/scripts/format.py#L1024-L1025), [board sync](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/scripts/board.py#L578-L582) and the [pull request fetch](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/artifacts/pull-request.md#L523-L539).

## Proposal

- **Fixes land in workflow-server first.**
  Each fix is a task row, merged into `workspace` through its epic base as any delivery is.
- **The extraction waits for the fixes.**
  I16's row that extracts the skill names these fixes as its prerequisite, so the extraction is cut from a `workspace` commit holding every one.
- **Faults found later join the plan.**
  A fault found before the extraction becomes a further task row, delivered ahead of the extraction like the rest.
- **A feature the skill must carry joins too.**
  A feature a workspace needs before the extraction, such as delivery lanes, is an epic of this initiative and lands ahead of the extraction as a fix does.

## Work Breakdown

| Epic | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1598) | Pre-Cutover Fixes | AC1 | | ✓ |
| [E01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | Skill Style | AC1 | | |
| [E02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1615) | Skill Separation | AC1 | [E01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | |
| [E03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1625) | Delivery Lanes | AC1 | | ✓ |

| [E04](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1654) | Delivery Failure Recovery | AC1 | [E01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Every Work Planner fix and feature planned here is in the history of the workflow-server `workspace` commit the skill's extraction is cut from, as `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows for each one's merge commit.

## Non-Goals

- It does not change the skill's layout, script paths or priority source, which the move to the new repository settles.
- It does not fix a fault found after the extraction is cut.

## References

- **R1.** [I16 Work Planner Home](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform-skills/issues/1) — the skill's move to prosiform-skills, whose extraction waits for these fixes.
- **R2.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes) — the decisions, the goal trace, the review and each task's work item.
- **R3.** [Work Planner at the planned revision](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner) — the skill the fixes change.

- **R4.** [Delivery failure recovery plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-06-1597-delivery-failure-recovery/design.md) — inherited readiness and refusal gaps, owning components, atomic unit and regression evidence.

e02.title: [I17:E02] Skill Separation: Every Rule in One Home Before the Extraction

labels.name: type:epic
labels.description: A phase-sized body of work

labels.name: theme:planning
labels.description: How Work Is Planned and Tracked

labels.name: priority: 6
labels.description: Queue rank. A larger number runs first.

e02.body:
## Overview

The work-planner skill gains SOLID guidelines fitted to its architecture, and the whole skill is audited and fixed against them in workflow-server before the skill's extraction is cut. Artifact and protocol files own their subjects, callable operations and command specifications; links select those capabilities and their required context. Each rule has one owning file or script module, and no general file names a specific kind of work, so the skill moves to prosiform-skills already separated.

## Problem

- **No separation grain is defined.** The guidelines define an artifact as one shape and a protocol as one change. They say nothing of how files encapsulate, extend or depend on one another.
  - Open–closed is stated only for the issue-body family: "the common file names no kind".
- **General files enumerate kinds of work.** The delivery plan, Deliver mode, pull request, board queue and Task Merge each name hot-fixes and branch on them.
  - Adding a kind means editing every general file again.
- **Scripts branch on kinds inline.**
  The delivery and board-queue scripts run hot-fix paths beside the epic paths.
- **Fields carry hidden behavior.**
  Board Delivery’s Status Changes computes status and membership decisions from delivery evidence and restricts permitted writes inside a field definition. Similar sections can conceal derivation or execution behind declarative wording.
- **Required reads are circular and broad.**
  A prerequisite cycle spans Board Delivery, Board Queue, Delivery Branches, Delivery Plan and related artifact modules. Whole-file imports pull unrelated command bodies into Standup and Understand before their selected operations run.
- **Retained preparation can reach creation.**
  Unit Dispatch accepts retained preparations but its session-preparation step calls Create Task Worktree unconditionally. A capacity-only resume can attempt to recreate the recorded branch and checkout.
- **Policy contexts can disagree.**
  Advance decision recording, backlog cascades, diagram sizing and hot-fix finding scope have competing readings. An ownership move alone cannot settle which inputs and outcomes a rule governs.
- **No map of the breaches.**
  Nobody has audited the whole skill, so the remaining breaches and their owning homes are unknown.

## Proposal

- **Files own subjects and capabilities.** An artifact or protocol file owns one subject or coordinated change, and callers select its operations or command specifications by link.
  - Commands precedes Fields and owns the enriched invocation and explicit I/O contract. Callers Run command specifications directly where no substantive procedure is needed.
  - Fields are the file's state and public shape. Nested calls keep selections, conditions and continuation without repeating I/O inventories.
  - Prerequisites identify context required before use, with common context separated from context selected by a particular operation.
- **SOLID guidelines first.** The first task adds a SOLID section to the skill's guidelines.
  - Single responsibility: one reason to change per file.
  - Open–closed: a new kind is a new file, and general files name no kind.
  - Liskov substitution: every kind fills an interface operation with the same contract.
  - Interface segregation: small callable capabilities, common prerequisites justified for every entry they govern, and conditional context reached at its point of use.
  - Dependency inversion: general files never link down to a kind, and kinds are listed in one registry.
  - Each file-type section links that section rather than restating it.
  - Define the required-before-use context graph separately from execution calls and ordinary field references. Its edges name their entry condition, required content and reason; the graph is acyclic. Reading a mode as a document retains the existing rule about loading its prerequisites only when invoked.
  - Fields define shapes and invariants; operations own derivation, execution, refusals and continuation. The audit distinguishes legitimate conditional constraints from hidden transformations.
- **Audit against the guidelines.** The second task reviews every artifact, mode, protocol and script against the guidelines' audit questions.
  - It records each breach in the planning record with its file, the guideline it breaks and the home that owns it. Every Fields section is classified; Board Delivery’s Status Changes is the confirmed starting finding. Candidates record the supplied evidence, produced decision, owning subject and disposition.
  - Classify every prerequisite edge by source section, target boundary, entry condition and necessity. Record required common context, context selected by a call, field definitions read at use and redundant preloads. Trace Standup, Revise and Understand from stable source revisions, including their consumer-specific context.
- **Fix rows from the audit.**
  The fix tasks take the audit's findings by concern, and each is split into one row per implementation component before dispatch. Each row carries its observing regressions, and parallel rows never edit the same file.
- **Bounded prerequisite reads.** Apply the reviewed edge dispositions to remove circular and unrelated preload requirements while retaining necessary common context, selected command contracts, authorization and evidence gates. Keep each rule at its owning subject; a visited-set workaround or an instruction to ignore an import does not settle an ownership or read-boundary defect.
  - Fixed routes supply complete, untruncated common and selected-operation context before use. Paired fresh-context trials use pinned source and executable captured fixtures; each trial records actual reads, omissions, unrelated content and prerequisite reuse.
- **Board Status artifact.** A new `board-status.md` owns the proposed status-change shape and the operations that derive and validate that change. Board Delivery gathers evidence, applies changes and confirms saved state. Board Queue retains priority/readiness decisions; lifecycle rules stay with their owning subjects.
  - The artifact, Board Delivery and Hot-fix consumer changes share one pull request so moved contracts, caller links and `○`, `●`, `ƒ` roles remain valid together. Existing status, membership, assignee, review-evidence and write-scope behavior is preserved.
- **Candidate detection and regression evidence.** Checker fixtures include the actual Status Changes text, structurally different hidden-transform examples and valid conditional field constraints. Diagnostics identify file, heading, evidence and candidate operation/owner; semantic classification is confirmed in the audit.
  - Extracted behavior and prerequisite fixes carry regression coverage in their own pull requests. The final checker task adds reusable candidate detection and prerequisite diagnostics with positive/negative fixtures; wording keywords alone do not establish a violation.
  - Cycle diagnostics name source/target sections and a closed witness path. Scope diagnostics are conservative review candidates unless a declared context contract proves the mismatch. Valid conditional prerequisites, ordinary definition cycles and intentional execution retries are controls.
- **Verified retained-preparation route.** After the separation diagnostics are available, reconcile Unit Dispatch with the existing automatic-dispatch correction in #1631 and [PR #1645](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1645). Creation records the preparation head; a retained preparation selects the owning read-only worktree validation, using the recorded checkout identity and current hold/start evidence. Keep that identity contract and its executable validation in Delivery Branches, with selection and continuation in Unit Dispatch.
  - Verify the separated route with the completed prerequisite diagnostics and capacity-wait/resume fixtures. A mismatch retains the checkout and hold, blocks that unit, and starts no worker. Successful reuse reaches the existing start gate once; new work still follows creation.
  - Reuse the upstream implementation and observing tests. Defects in that implementation are corrected in its owning pull request; this task reconciles its protocol calls and verifies their composition with the separated skill.
- **Policy clarification decisions.** The audit includes the four inherited ambiguities in the [policy clarification plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/policy-clarifications.md). Each candidate has its exact context, current prose and observed behavior, recommended interpretation, owning contract and distinguishing scenarios.
  - Audit and proposed interpretations are authorized; each policy interpretation is confirmed before its fix is dispatched. Distinguish a wording conflict from different rules governing different contexts.
  - The ownership fixes apply confirmed interpretations and their observing regressions together, with one canonical rule and links from callers. Split fixes into exact component rows before dispatch and reconcile shared files with the delivery-recovery plan.
  - Use the Style epic's field ledger and review evidence as the starting inventory, then refresh against its delivered revision; a resolved presentation or field-boundary issue is not repeated as an open defect.
- **Behaviour.**
  Ownership-only fixes preserve outcomes. A confirmed policy clarification records its permitted outcome differences and observing scenarios before implementation; extraction regressions compare against that clarified baseline.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W01 | SOLID guidelines, Fields and read-context boundaries | AC1 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | | | |
| W02 | Audit ownership, Fields and prerequisite boundaries | AC2, AC10, AC17 | W01 | | | |
| W03 | Generic prose in general artifacts and modes | AC3 | W02 | | | |
| W04 | Generic interfaces in general scripts | AC4 | W02 | | | |
| W05 | Rule ownership and bounded prerequisite reads | AC5, AC11, AC12 | W02 | | | |
| [W06](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/w06.md) | Board Status artifact and transformations | AC6 | W03, W04, W05 | W07, W08 | | |
| [W07](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/w07.md) | Board Delivery calls the status operations | AC7 | W03, W04, W05 | W06, W08 | | |
| [W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/w08.md) | Hot-fix uses the extracted status contract | AC8 | W03, W04, W05 | W06, W07 | | |
| [W09](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/w09.md) | Detect Fields behavior and prerequisite violations | AC9, AC13 | W06, W07, W08 |  | | |
| [W10](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/w10.md) | Retained preparations select verified worktree reuse | AC14, AC15, AC16 | W09, [#1631](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1631) | | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The skill's guidelines state each SOLID principle for artifact, protocol and mode files, including the boundary between field constraints and transformations, and every file-type section links to their owning definitions, read in the skill guidelines.
- [ ] **AC2.** Every breach of those guidelines in the skill's artifacts, modes, protocols and scripts is listed with its file, its guideline and its owning home, as the audit in the planning record shows.
- [ ] **AC3.** No general artifact, mode or protocol names a specific kind of work as a case it handles, checked by a search of the skill.
- [ ] **AC4.** No general script branches on a kind of work, and each kind's logic lives in its own module, checked by a search of the scripts.
- [ ] **AC5.** Each rule the audit lists is stated in its owning home alone, and every consumer follows that linked contract, as source searches and approved scenario fixtures show.

- [ ] **AC6.** Board Status owns the proposed status-change contract and its callable transformations in its own artifact, checked by the installed model and document readers.
- [ ] **AC7.** Board Delivery obtains status decisions through the owning operations with the same status, membership, assignee and write-scope outcomes for identical evidence, as its extraction regression fixtures and caller checks show.
- [ ] **AC8.** Hot-fix consumes the extracted status contract through its owning operation with the same closure and status outcomes for identical evidence, as its extraction regression fixtures and field/caller checks show.
- [ ] **AC9.** The Work Planner checks identify the actual Status Changes example and representative hidden transformations in Fields as review candidates while accepting legitimate schemas, conditional invariants and literal examples, as positive/negative fixtures and semantic review show.
- [ ] **AC10.** Every Fields section has a classified boundary/ownership disposition in the audit, including Status Changes and recorded similar candidates.

- [ ] **AC11.** The required-before-use context graph is acyclic for every supported Work Planner entry path, as the audited prerequisite graph and cycle regression fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC12.** Each representative reading trace conforms to its reviewed per-entry context contract, as repeated fresh-context Standup, Revise and Understand trials with pinned sources and captured inputs show.
- [ ] **AC13.** The prerequisite checks distinguish invalid before-use graphs from valid scoped reads, as positive/negative fixtures containing the measured artifact cycle, conditional prerequisites, field-reference cycles and execution retries show.

- [ ] **AC14.** Unit Dispatch selects the owning worktree-validation capability for a retained preparation and creation for a new unit, preserving each retained checkout's recorded branch and full preparation head, as protocol-routing checks and real-git reuse fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC15.** An absent or mismatched repository registration, branch, full preparation head, or clean tracked/untracked state blocks retained reuse without changing the checkout or starting a worker, as negative fixtures and before/after repository snapshots show.
- [ ] **AC16.** A capacity-only wait resumes with the same published planning record, retained unit context and confirmed hold, and starts exactly one worker only after current batch/session/capacity validation passes, as an ordered wait/resume event fixture and the separated route's prerequisite checks show.

- [ ] **AC17.** Every policy ambiguity in the clarification catalog has an approved decision record, as the ownership audit and its linked decision evidence show.

## References

- **R1.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes) — the decisions, the audit and each task's work item.
- **R2.** [SOLID guidelines draft](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/solid-guidelines.md) — the guidelines the first task lands, with the class model and the audit questions.
- **R3.** [Delivery Units](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1614) — the delivery-path breach that prompted this review.
- **R4.** [Work Planner at the planned revision](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/756aaf9f53f884b1da120e990ec9524a936aa4b2/skills/work-planner) — the skill the review audits.

- **R5.** [Fields and transformations plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/fields-and-transformations.md) — confirmed finding, ownership, candidate audit, atomic extraction and regression matrix.

- **R6.** [Prerequisite cleanup plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/prerequisite-cleanup.md) — measured cycle, per-entry context contracts, task allocation and structural/live verification.

- **R7.** [Retained preparation plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/retained-preparation.md) — owning capabilities, upstream reconciliation, criterion ownership and safe-resume regression matrix.

- **R8.** [Delivery failure recovery design](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-06-1597-delivery-failure-recovery/design.md) — the ownership audit incorporates these planned Deliver Mode, Pull Request and Epic Integration corrections and resolves shared-file contention when its fix rows acquire exact components.

- **R9.** [Policy clarification plan](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes/e02/policy-clarifications.md) — the four inherited ambiguities, decision gates, canonical owners, task allocation and distinguishing scenario matrix.

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: type:epic

labels.name: priority: 6

e00.body:
## Overview

This epic delivers each Work Planner fix found before the skill's extraction to its own repository, merged into `workspace` so the extraction carries it. Each fix is a task row, and a fault found later joins as a further row.

## Problem

The skill carries faults its own planning and sync runs have exposed.

- **Planning takes a branch the record forbids.**
  [Plan Mode](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L42-L43) opens a draft discussion pull request from a planning branch, while the [planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/artifacts/planning-record.md#L153) states the engineering branch takes no further branch.
- **Draft bodies sit outside the record.**
  The [Bodies convention](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/SKILL.md#L96) keeps body files outside the repository, so a plan's drafts are not part of its committed record.
- **A not-planned epic has no rule.**
  [Initiative rows](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#L143-L153) say nothing of an epic closed as not planned; only [task rows another issue takes](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#L267-L268) leave a table.
- **A criterion gap asks for a decision.**
  The [format check](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/scripts/format.py#L1024-L1025) asks to decide criterion labels not numbered from one without a gap. When #1427 closed as not planned, #1166 dropped its row by hand.
- **Uncited closed items stay on the board.**
  [Board sync](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/scripts/board.py#L578-L582) removes an item closed other than as completed only when a plan body cites it, so #1427 and #1475 were deleted from their board by hand.
- **Sync misses untitled pull requests.**
  [Read Initiative Pull Requests](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/artifacts/pull-request.md#L95-L102) keeps only [titles carrying the initiative prefix](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/785a5ee8c715b802498aa41712e0489425a22cfa/skills/work-planner/artifacts/pull-request.md#L523-L539), so older task pull requests that #1166's epic rows link went unread until fetched by hand.

## Proposal

- **Planning commits straight to engineering.**
  Every planning artifact, draft bodies and work items included, is committed to the engineering branch in its planning record's folder. Planning opens no branch and no pull request.
- **A not-planned epic leaves its initiative.**
  Its row and the criteria only it covers are removed, and References name where its work went. Criterion numbers other work cites are kept, and the format check accepts the gap.
- **Every item closed other than as completed leaves the board.**
  Board sync applies that status to each such item on the board, whether or not a plan body cites it.
- **Sync reads pull requests by their links.**
  The fetch selects each pull request a row or a Development link of the plan names, whatever its title.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1605) | Planning commits directly to engineering | AC1, AC2, AC3 | | | ✓ |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1602) | Not-planned epic leaves its initiative | AC4, AC5, AC6 | | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1603) | Board sync removes uncited not-planned items | AC7 | | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1607) | Sync reads every linked pull request | AC8 | | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Plan Mode writes every draft body and work item into its planning record's folder, as the skill's fixture suite checks against the mode's procedure.
- [x] **AC2.** Plan Mode publishes its planning record by committing it to the engineering branch and pushing that branch, as the skill's fixture suite checks against the mode's procedure.
- [x] **AC3.** No skill file names a planning branch or a discussion pull request, as a search of the skill's files shows.
- [x] **AC4.** An initiative row whose epic is closed as not planned is removed with every criterion only that row covers, as the initiative body's Work Breakdown conditions state.
- [x] **AC5.** An initiative that removes such a row names where its work went in References, as the initiative body's References conditions state.
- [x] **AC6.** The format check reports no finding on criterion labels that ascend with a gap, as the format check's fixture suite shows.
- [x] **AC7.** Board sync removes every board item closed other than as completed, whether or not a plan body cites it, as the board fixture suite shows for a cited and an uncited item.
- [x] **AC8.** Sync's pull request records hold every pull request a row or a Development link of the plan names, whatever its title, as the sync fixture suite shows for a linked pull request whose title carries no initiative prefix.

## References

- **R1.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes) — the decisions, the goal trace, the review and each task's work item.

e01.title: [I17:E01] Skill Style: The Groundwork for Prosiform Compliance

labels.name: type:epic
labels.description: A phase-sized body of work

labels.name: theme:planning
labels.description: How Work Is Planned and Tracked

labels.name: priority: 7
labels.description: Queue rank. A larger number runs first.

e01.body:
## Overview The work-planner skill takes the file style its prosiform form will need, laying the groundwork for prosiform compliance before the skill's extraction is cut. The style is the one the example skill under `.project/main/example` shows. That example is an older work-planner and serves as a structural style reference only: no content carries over from it. Command presentation follows the linked Graph Index example in R5. Prerequisites sections stay, and no prosiform metadata is added. ## Problem - **Steps are list items.** Every procedure is a numbered list with bold leads, so a step has no heading to link and no place for its own detail. - **Commands sit apart from the steps that run them.** Artifacts hold a `## Commands` section that their operations reach by link. - **Inputs and outputs lack explicit roles.** Operation prose does not consistently link every consumed or provided value to its owning Field, leaving part of the caller contract implied. - **SKILL.md carries the rules.** The rules and conventions that bind every mode, and the deployment values, sit in SKILL.md and the guidelines rather than in files of their own. - **The style model describes the installed layout.** The current declarations and checks do not define the proposed heading-based steps, linked contracts and HTML command blocks. ## Proposal - **Per-skill style model.** The skill's own guidelines, `structure.json` and `rules.json` state the new model, and the shared checker reads each skill's declared model. - The shared guidelines and every other skill keep their current shape. - Checker support is proven against specimen skills before document conversion. The final task adopts Work Planner's new guidelines and model declarations once every conversion is complete; the installed declarations govern the live checks until that adoption. - **Entry files.** SKILL.md keeps its opening, Modes and Dependencies. - `rules.md` holds the rules that bind every mode, `conventions.md` the conventions, and `configuration.md` the deployment values, each built from the live skill's own text. - **Steps as sub-sections.** Each step is a heading of its position and action. A step with multiple contained instruction or detail items bullets every item; a single item is plain text. - Calls use Apply for an artifact operation and Follow for a mode, protocol or child section. - Each mode and protocol opens with the preamble line that links Rules, Conventions and, for a mode, Outcomes. - **Commands in steps.** Each command sits in the step that runs it, with its execution location and any meaningful usage conditions. Linked command arguments establish their contracts without a repeated parameter list in prose. Value-format, payload and output examples are fenced data under the owning linked Field; executing steps carry the generic invocation. No artifact keeps a `## Commands` section. - Command and tool-access invocations use raw HTML `
…
` blocks, matching the specific R5 step. Contract-backed input names are bold Markdown links inside the block, using role-tagged `[**argument**](#argument-contract "○")`. Long shell invocations use backslash-newline continuations at token boundaries, grouping options with their values while preserving literal syntax and argument order. Shell quoting follows the value type: validated shell-safe numbers/identifiers and fixed safe literals are unquoted; variable paths, refs, free text and query expressions retain their required quoting. - Checker fixtures accept this HTML command form and its resolving argument links, and reject Markdown-fenced command invocations. The example supplies presentation only; its tool names, graph behavior, content and metadata are outside this migration. - **Inputs, outputs and contracts.** Each operation links every consumed input and provided output to its owning `###` Field where it is used, in natural step prose or an executing command. Prose retains semantic conditions and caller-facing results without repeating command bindings. Markdown link titles mark `"○"` and `"●"` at those uses; links to called operations, protocols and procedures carry `"ƒ"`. Outputs use Provide, with a distinct provision step when needed. `rules.md` defines the tag meanings, and the guidelines require an independent completeness check against steps, commands, calls, conditions and results. Performed-operation contract verification remains a future feature. - **What does not change.** The skill's behaviour, its Prerequisites sections and its frontmatter stay as they are. - No prosiform metadata, no `pf` instruction and no prosiform link marks, which need its grammar to place. - No file or rule is taken from the example's content. ## Work Breakdown | Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1640) | Per-skill style model and checker | AC1 | | | | ✓ | | [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1642) | Rules, conventions and configuration files | AC2 | W01 | | | ✓ | | [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1643) | Modes in the new style | AC3 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1644) | Protocols in the new style | AC4 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1646) | Issue and body artifacts in the new style | AC5 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W06](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1651) | Board, queue, planning and review artifacts restyled | AC6 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W07](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1647) | Delivery, branch and pull-request artifacts restyled | AC7 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1652) | Activate the Work Planner style model | AC8 | W03, W04, W05, W06, W07 | | | ✓ | ## Acceptance Criteria - [x] **AC1.** `check_skill_files.py` validates specimen declarations of the proposed Work Planner style model, including its command style, as acceptance/rejection fixtures show. - [x] **AC2.** SKILL.md holds only its opening, Modes and Dependencies, and `rules.md`, `conventions.md` and `configuration.md` hold what binds every mode, checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC3.** Every mode states its steps as sub-sections, opens with the preamble line and calls through Apply and Follow, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC4.** Every protocol states its steps as sub-sections, opens with the preamble line and calls through Apply and Follow, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC5.** Every issue and body artifact runs its commands inside its steps and links every input and output at its actual use in step prose or an executing command with its role title, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC6.** Every board, queue, planning and review artifact runs its commands inside its steps and links every input and output at its actual use in step prose or an executing command with its role title, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC7.** Every delivery, branch and pull-request artifact runs its commands inside its steps and links every input and output at its actual use in step prose or an executing command with its role title, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC8.** The Work Planner guidelines, `structure.json` and `rules.json` declare the new style model over the converted skill, with zero findings from Check Skill Files over `skills/work-planner`. ## References - **R1.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes) — the decisions, the artifact grouping and each task's work item. - **R2.** [Example skill](https://github.com/m2ux/md-composer/tree/00f166920ec242f3565376e06a8838de72f8dc34/example/work-planner) — the older work-planner whose file style this epic adopts; style only. - **R3.** [Example guidelines](https://github.com/m2ux/md-composer/blob/00f166920ec242f3565376e06a8838de72f8dc34/example/guidelines.md) — the shared guidelines that state that style. - **R4.** [Work Planner at the migration baseline](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/03d353300ca4804194fd50d316d73e3bf1270d1d/skills/work-planner) — the skill this epic restyles. - **R5.** [HTML command-style example](https://github.com/shieldedtech/midnight-agent-eng/blob/a710a42e82df7f18b27f8a6cfa4b6e9c801df903/skills/finding-classifier/artifacts/graph-index.md#1-fetch-the-first-inventory-page) — the specific command presentation adopted by this migration; style only.

e03.title: [I17:E03] Delivery Lanes: Each Task Row Carries Its Lane

labels.name: type:epic
labels.description: A phase-sized body of work

labels.name: theme:planning
labels.description: How Work Is Planned and Tracked

e03.body:
## Overview

A board can be delivered by more than one session at once, each serving its own lane of task rows. Each row carries its lane as a bare index in the epic Work Breakdown table, Plan mode assigns it, and a Deliver run naming a lane takes its lane’s rows and unlaned rows. The epic lands before the skill’s extraction, so the skill moves with lanes.

## Problem

- **The live task table has no lane column.**
  Its Task, Description, Coverage, Depends on, Joins and Done cells contain no lane assignment.
- **Work-item declarations split the row’s plan.**
  The epic base’s Work Item artifact defines a separate Lane declaration, so the task table alone cannot show or supply a row’s lane.
- **Every session sees one queue.**
  The delivery survey offers available units by priority and dependencies, so two sessions on one board can select the same unit.
- **A label cannot carry it.**
  A label marks an issue, while task rows in one epic can belong to different lanes and have no task issue.

## Proposal

- **The task table owns the lane.**
  Its columns are `Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done`. Lane contains a bare decimal index such as `2`; an empty cell is unlaned.
- **A lane is an opaque board-wide index.**
  The same index names one lane across the theme board. Its cell contains the index alone.
- **The request names the run’s lane.**
  A Deliver request states its lane each time. A request naming none is offered only unlaned units.
- **A laned run also admits unlaned work.**
  A run is offered its lane’s units and unlaned units, ordered by priority. Hot-fix units are unlaned.
- **Plan mode writes the task cells.**
  It asks whether the initiative uses lanes, proposes each row’s index for confirmation and passes the confirmed values to Populate Epic Issue Body.
- **Joined rows share one lane.**
  Their Lane cells carry the same index or are all empty. The dependency check refuses a split unit, settled by changing a lane or unjoining.
- **Readers use the issue body.**
  Dependency checks, delivery and queue reporting use one task-table lane reader. Work-item files supply components and implementation plans.
- **Table operations preserve lanes.**
  Format validation checks bare indices, and normalization, reservation, release, linking and Done ticks preserve the Lane cell.
- **The queue reports unit lanes.**
  Board Queue reports each Ready unit’s lane from its existing issue snapshots, and Advance carries those report lines.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1626) | Work item declares an optional lane | | | | | ✓ |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1628) | Task table carries the lane column | AC11 | | W03 | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1628) | Work item holds its component declaration | AC12 | W01 | W02 | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1629) | Joined rows share one lane | AC3 | W02 | W05, W06 | | ✓ |
| [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1629) | Dependency check reads task table lanes | AC4 | W02 | W04, W06 | | ✓ |
| [W06](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1629) | Lane cells validate and survive table writes | AC13, AC14 | W02 | W04, W05 | | ✓ |
| [W07](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1632) | Delivery plan admits units by lane | AC2 | W02 | W08 | | ✓ |
| [W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1632) | Available-work survey filters units by lane | AC5 | W05 | W07 | | ✓ |
| [W09](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1634) | Deliver mode passes the requested lane | AC6 | W07 | | | ✓ |
| [W10](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1633) | Plan mode writes task row lanes | AC7 | W04 | | | ✓ |
| [W11](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1637) | Board queue reports Ready units' lanes | AC8 | W07 | W12 | | ✓ |
| [W12](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1637) | Board-queue script prints Ready unit lanes | AC9 | W05 | W11 | | ✓ |
| [W13](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1638) | Advance mode reports Ready unit lanes | AC10 | W11 | | | ✓ |
| [W14](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1635) | Cross-epic joins receive bounded diagnostics | AC15 | W05 | | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC2.** The Delivery Plan artifact states lane admission from task-table Lane cells: a run naming an index is offered units in that lane and unlaned units, a run naming none is offered only unlaned units, priority orders admitted units, and each unit line names its lane, as a read of the artifact shows.
- [x] **AC3.** The Dependency Graph artifact states that joined rows share one Lane index or all have empty Lane cells, and a split unit is refused with moving a lane or unjoining as its resolutions, as a read of the artifact shows.
- [x] **AC4.** The dependency check reads and validates the task-table Lane cells and refuses a joined unit with different lane values, naming each row and its lane, as test_deps.py fixtures with equal, different, empty and malformed Lane cells show.
- [x] **AC5.** The available-work survey reads task-table Lane cells and offers only the units admitted by the requested lane, including laned rows with no work-item link, as test_deliver.py fixtures with two lanes and unlaned rows show.
- [x] **AC6.** Deliver mode passes the lane its request names to every Plan Available Work call, passes none when the request names none, and stores no lane per session, as a read of the mode shows.
- [x] **AC7.** Plan mode asks whether an initiative uses lanes, proposes each row’s lane for confirmation and passes each confirmed index to Populate Epic Issue Body for its Lane cell, as a read of the mode shows.
- [x] **AC8.** The Board Queue artifact states that each Ready unit’s reported lane comes from its task-table Lane cells in the supplied issue bodies, as a read of the artifact shows.
- [x] **AC9.** The board-queue script reports each Ready unit’s task-table lane while producing identical placement calls for the same delivery state, as test_board_queue.py fixtures with laned and unlaned rows show.
- [x] **AC10.** Advance mode reports each Ready unit’s lane from the returned board queue lines, as a read of the mode shows.
- [x] **AC11.** The Epic Issue Body artifact defines and populates the exact task-table columns Task, Description, Coverage, Depends on, Joins, Lane, Done, with Lane holding a bare board-wide index such as 2 or an empty unlaned cell, as an artifact read and specimen row population show.
- [x] **AC12.** The Work Item artifact’s population inputs, template, fields and section rules describe Component as its declaration and contain no Lane declaration path, as a read and search of the artifact show.
- [x] **AC13.** The issue-format check rejects populated Lane cells that are not bare indices, as test_format.py fixtures for valid, empty, marked-up and prose cells show.
- [x] **AC14.** Valid and empty Lane values stay attached to their task rows through normalization, reservation, release and delivery recording, as test_format.py, test_deliver.py and test_sync.py round-trip fixtures show.
- [x] **AC15.** Joins entries outside their row’s epic produce a row-specific nonzero dependency-check result before epic-priority calculation, as CLI regression fixtures for the pinned reciprocal-join reproducer and ordinary same-epic joins show.

## References

- **R1.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes) — the decisions, the dependency report and each task's work item.
- **R2.** [prosiform I10 Evaluation and Checks](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/464) — the initiative whose two delivery sessions wait on the lane filter.
- **R3.** [Work Planner at the planned revision](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/b2844c821ce800ed3d12735bdf339049594e5ec5/skills/work-planner) — the skill this epic changes.

- **R4.** [Cross-epic join input](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1630) — the pinned unsupported-input priority recursion and its bounded-diagnostic fix.

e04.title: [I17:E04] Delivery Failure Recovery: Verified Draft and Merge Outcomes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: type:epic
labels.description: A phase-sized body of work

labels.name: theme:planning
labels.description: How Work Is Planned and Tracked

labels.name: priority: 6
labels.description: Queue rank. A larger number runs first.

e04.body:
## Overview

Work Planner leaves failed readiness and merge attempts in an explicit, verified state. Hot-fix review failure withdraws ready state, and epic integration follows the owning merge result without unintended retries or success assertions.

## Problem

- Hot-fix readiness can fail after marking a pull request ready, while the repair route promises draft state without an explicit restoring write and readback.
- Epic integration treats refusal generically although the owning merge operation distinguishes harness denial and GitHub refusal, and its final readback assumes a merge.
- The merge-permission field describes task-to-epic-base authorization while the shared operation handles further delivery targets.

## Proposal

Deliver Mode selects the existing draft command and confirms its result before hot-fix repair. Pull Request owns explicit merge outcomes and the permission boundary; Epic Integration consumes them with bounded retry and terminal handoff/refusal branches. One atomic unit changes the shared merge contract and its epic caller. Behavior is verified with ordered calls and terminal-result fixtures, including restoration failure and each refusal source.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-06-1597-delivery-failure-recovery/w01.md) | Confirm draft state after failed hot-fix readiness | AC1, AC2, AC3 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | | | |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-06-1597-delivery-failure-recovery/w02.md) | Explicit merge outcomes and permission boundaries | AC4, AC5 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | W03 | | |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-06-1597-delivery-failure-recovery/w03.md) | Epic continuation follows the merge outcome | AC6, AC7 | [E01:W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1616) | W02 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A hot-fix validation failure after a ready write selects draft restoration and confirms current draft state before repair, as ordered failure-route fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A failed restoration or disagreeing readback produces an explicit unresolved discrepancy without claiming draft state or reaching merge/In Review, as negative fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** Passing hot-fix review and ready readback reaches normal merge exactly once, as a positive route fixture shows.
- [ ] **AC4.** Merge Delivery Pull Request provides distinct confirmed-merge, human-handoff, harness-denial and GitHub-refusal outcomes with current head/target evidence, as contract and outcome fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** Merge Permission describes the existing authorization/capability boundary for each supported delivery target without authorizing protection bypass or widening harness permission, as source review against configured target requirements and permission-denial fixtures shows.
- [ ] **AC6.** Epic integration terminates human handoff and harness denial without same-run retry or merged-success readback, as ordered negative fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC7.** Epic integration retries GitHub refusal only within the existing bound after fresh verification, terminates repeated refusal, and confirms merged head/target/commit only after a confirmed merge, as route fixtures show.

## References

- **R1.** [Recovery design](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-06-1597-delivery-failure-recovery/design.md) — source evidence, ownership, units and regression matrix.
